summary: Hans Küng worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University and Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum (~1948–1955), and Institut Catholique de Paris (~1955–1956). He held a post at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1996).

Hans Losch was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Munich (1921–1922) and the University of Bonn (1920–1927), studying under Hermann Jacobi and Willibald Kirfel in 1924. He held academic posts at the University of Bonn (1927, 1935, 1939, 1963–1967).

Hans Much worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at the universities of Marburg, Kiel, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Würzburg (Dr.med. by 1903). In 1919, he became Professor of Medicine at the University of Hamburg.

Hans Nordewin von Körber worked in sinology, tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Berlin, Bonn, Marburg (~1919–1921, Ph.D.), and Cambridge. He was Professor of Oriental Studies at the University of Southern California (~1928–1950) and founded The Divine Word Foundation (1962).

Hans Reichelt worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna (1896–1898) under Bühler, Meringer, and Müller, and at Giessen (~1898–1900) under Bartholomae. His posts included Chernivtsi (1911), Graz (1920), and Hamburg (1926–1929).

Hans Schacht specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin (by 1890). He taught at École Normale Cantonale de Lausanne (1895–1912) and Gymnase de la Cité (1912), and served as PD at the University of Lausanne (1903–1933).

Hans T. Bakker specialized in Indology and religious studies, studying under Jacob Ensink (~1975–1984). He held posts at Utrecht University (~1982–1987), the University of Groningen (~1987–2013), and the British Museum (curator, retired 2014).
Hans Urs von Balthasar was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Zurich (~1923–1928) and under Bernhard Geiger from 1924 to 1926.
Hans West worked in Indology. He studied at Odense Katedralskole and served as rector at the Danish School in Christiansted in 1788.

Hans Wilhelm Haussig was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied under Robert Bleichsteiner and at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1935–1939). He held professorial posts at Free University of Berlin (1956, 1968) and Ruhr University Bochum (1969–1982).
Hans Windisch was a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (~1929–1935), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1935).

Hans Wirtz was an Indologist and sinologist. He studied at the University of Munich (1887), University of Bonn (1889–1894) under Hermann Jacobi in 1889, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He later taught at the University of Cologne (1922–1929).

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit worked in religious, Iranian/Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Augustana Divinity School, Tübingen under Helmuth von Glasenapp, Bonn under Gustav Mensching, and Harvard. He was habilitated (1968) and served as Direktor (1972) at the University of Bonn.
Hans-Joachim Rassat was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Tübingen under Helmuth von Glasenapp from approximately 1951 to 1955, completing his Ph.D. there.

Hans-Rudolf Kantor is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at the University of Delhi, National Taiwan University, and University of Bonn. He held positions at Huafan University, Tamkang University, Fo Guang Shan, Fo Guang University, and National Chengchi University.

Hans-Ulrich Rieker worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied as a disciple under Anagarika Govinda (~1952–1979). In 1952 he founded Arya Maitreya Mandala, serving as its leader from ~1952 to 1964.
Hans-Werbin Köhler was an Indology scholar. He studied under Eduard Hermann and completed his studies under doctoral supervisor Ernst Waldschmidt by 1948.
Hansjakob Seiler was a linguist who studied under Manu Leumann from ~1940 to 1947. He held a post at the University of Cologne from ~1959 to 1986.

Hanung Kim is a scholar in tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a Master's degree at Columbia University and earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.
Har Bilas Sarda worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1886–1888) and served as a judge at the Court of Small Causes, Ajmer (~1923–1924).
